subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw scope issue #45771 as observability-only provider pace context first, opt-in runtime throttling now, or plugin/API groundwork before any core enforcement?
rationale: The request crosses provider-specific usage semantics, auth/session routing, new config, persisted state, and autonomous scheduling behavior, so code inspection cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Ship pace visibility first
options.body: Extend provider usage hooks and status/session_status with pace context while leaving autonomous throttling disabled until the signal quality and recovery UX are proven.

options.title: Build opt-in enforcement now
options.body: Add explicit pace config and persisted state with conservative default-off throttling, accepting a larger upgrade-sensitive runtime change.

options.title: Start with plugin/API hooks
options.body: Define provider/plugin contracts for richer quota and cost signals before deciding whether core owns any pacing policy.

recommendation.title: Ship pace visibility first
recommendation.body: Extend provider usage hooks and status/session_status with pace context while leaving autonomous throttling disabled until the signal quality and recovery UX are proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the provider usage tracking path and has the strongest current history across the status/gateway usage surfaces that would own the first product boundary decision.
